info.bio: Sylvester James (nació el 6 de septiembre de 1947 en Los Angeles, California y falleció el 16 de diciembre de 1988 en San Francisco, California)  fue un cantante de música disco. Conocido por cantar en falsette (a pesar de tener una voz de barítono), él también es considerado uno de los primeros fundadores del sonido Hi-NRG, junto a Patrick Cowley, recibiendo incluencias desde Europa, de grupos como Telex o musicos como Giorgio Moroder. Su abuela era el cantante de jazz Julia Morgan.

mentions.text: …«Boogie Fever», de The Sylvers, «Get Down Tonight», de KC and The Sunshine Band, y, sobre todo, el irresistible «Do You Wanna Funk», el hit de Sylvester producido por Patrick Cowley que arranca como un encierro de San Fermín, respondían a lo que años más tarde se conocería como el gag de la música…

Su oportunidad llegó cuando el cantante Sylvester le propuso participar como teclista en la grabación de su álbum, y así Step II (Fantasy, 1978) resultó un rotundo éxito internacional en gran parte…

podcast.title: AIDS Legacy and Philanthropy (1988)
podcast.body: Sylvester died of AIDS in 1988, leaving the royalties from all his work to HIV and AIDS charities in San Francisco, his adopted hometown. "Sylvester died of AIDS in 1988 and he left the money from the royalties of all of his work to HIV and AIDS charities in San Francisco."

podcast.title: Backed by Pointer Sisters (Early-Mid 70s)
podcast.body: The Pointer Sisters contributed backing vocals to recordings by Sylvester during the early to mid-70s. "In the early to mid 70s, the sisters backed up recordings by Bashaggs, Sylvester, Betty Davis, and on this recording, the solo album by Jefferson Airplane slash Jefferson Starship front woman Grace Slick."

podcast.title: Initial Dislike of Producer Emphasis
podcast.body: Sylvester was not a fan of disco, primarily disliking its emphasis on producers over artists. However, with the "Saturday Night Fever" phenomenon making disco an $8 billion industry, he decided to "cash in." "Sylvester was also not a big fan of disco because he didn't like the emphasis on the producer rather than the artist."

podcast.title: Unambiguous Gay Pride Icon
podcast.body: Sylvester occupied an unambiguous position on the disco spectrum, proudly and openly gay in the 1970s without costume or parody. Despite growing up with a Pentecostal Church mother who did not accept gayness, he left home at 15 to live with his grandmother due to his mother's non-acceptance, refusing to change who he was. "there is nothing ambiguous about Sylvester. He was not in costume. He was not a parody of a gay man. It was not easy to be out and proud if you were gay in the 1970s, but Sylvester was."
